title: Bram and the Promise
premise: Dominic Oyelaran, a romance novelist who has never believed in his own genre, returns to the island lighthouse town of Carrickmoor for his grandmother's eightieth birthday reunion, where every cousin arrives paired and smug. Desperate to deflect matchmaking, he recruits Bram Halloran, a quiet ferry mechanic with a reputation for fixing things that shouldn't be fixable, to pose as his boyfriend for one weekend. The fake date curdles into something real by dessert, but Dominic's instinct is to run: he has a deadline in London, a career built on emotional distance, and a family secret about the lighthouse's closure that could ruin his grandmother if exposed. When Dominic discovers Bram has been quietly fighting the ferry company's illegal shutdown of the winter route—the lifeline of the island—he must choose between protecting his family's silence and standing beside a man who refuses to look away from injustice. In the end, Dominic testifies at the maritime hearing, publishes his first honest novel, and stays past the last train, catching the last ferry of the season not as an escape but as a homecoming.
about_author: Lior Okonkwo is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent five years cataloguing lighthouse logs along the Atlantic coast before turning to fiction. They write love stories about people who mistake duty for destiny.

chapters.title: The Muscle That Lies
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. In his London flat, Dominic finishes a romance manuscript he privately disdains, lecturing his editor that love is trainable like any muscle. A summons arrives: Grandmother Adaeze's eightieth reunion at Carrickmoor lighthouse, partners expected. Emotional beat: wry self-protection masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Last Ferry Out
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram repairs the aging ferry Solace while the company posts notice of the winter route's cancellation. He organizes islanders in secret, careful to stay invisible to officials. Emotional beat: steadfast anger channeled into quiet competence.

chapters.title: A Reasonable Proposal
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. On the crossing to Carrickmoor, Dominic panics over the partner requirement and spots Bram working the deck. Over bad coffee, he offers money for a weekend pretense; Bram refuses payment but agrees—for reasons he doesn't say aloud. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity sparking.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. They negotiate cover-story details on the clifftop walk: no real names to cousins, no touching unless necessary, leave on Sunday's boat. Each rule feels like a wall being built. Emotional beat: playful tension undercut by mutual wariness.

chapters.title: The Reunion Begins
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The Oyelaran compound fills with cousins, their spouses, and Adaeze's imperious warmth. Dominic performs happiness; Bram plays his role with unnerving ease, charming even the hostile cousin Ngozi. Emotional beat: performance becoming indistinguishable from comfort.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. At the banquet, a toast forces Bram to speak about 'how we met,' and he improvises something so tender it silences the table—and Dominic. Their hands meet under the tablecloth and neither pulls away. Emotional beat: the fake date turning fatally real.

chapters.title: What the Lighthouse Remembers
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. The matriarch watches her grandson laugh genuinely for the first time in years, and recalls the night she kept the light burning alone through a storm that killed her husband. She suspects the boys are lying and decides to let them. Emotional beat: knowing tenderness.

chapters.title: Sunday Boat, Missed
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Sunday dawns; the plan says leave. Instead Dominic wakes to find Bram teaching his young nephew to mend nets, and lets the ferry go without him, inventing a deadline extension. Emotional beat: the first deliberate surrender.

chapters.title: The Shutdown Papers
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram shows Dominic the documents proving the ferry company falsified safety inspections to justify cancelling the winter route. He asks nothing of Dominic—yet. Emotional beat: trust offered without conditions.

chapters.title: Ink and Salt
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic realizes the scandal touches his late grandfather, who signed off on the original inspection under pressure. Exposing it could stain Adaeze's legacy. He urges Bram to drop it; they fight on the seawall. Emotional beat: love colliding with loyalty.

chapters.title: Ngozi Knows
chapters.summary: Ngozi's POV. Sharp-eyed Ngozi confronts Dominic: she's found no record of Bram anywhere in his life. She gives him until the family photo on Saturday to confess—or she will. Emotional beat: blackmail born of wounded protectiveness.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. A gale traps them together at the lighthouse; power fails, and they keep the old lamp lit by hand as Adaeze once did. In the dark, Bram tells Dominic why he fights for the ferry: his father drowned when the last route was cut decades ago. Emotional beat: grief shared becomes intimacy.

chapters.title: The Almost
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. After the storm, soaked and laughing in the lamp room, they nearly kiss—and Dominic retreats, citing the novel deadline, the hearing, everything. Bram accepts it too gracefully. Emotional beat: cowardice dressed as prudence.

chapters.title: Deadline in London
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Back in the city, Dominic tries to finish his manuscript and finds every page dishonest. His editor rejects the draft: 'You've written around the story again.' He rereads his own blurb-skepticism and hears Bram's voice in it. Emotional beat: craft forcing confession.

chapters.title: The Hearing Notice
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The maritime authority schedules the route review; Bram's petition needs witness testimony within ten days, or the shutdown stands. Island support wavers as the company threatens jobs. Emotional beat: a lone fight approaching its breaking point.

chapters.title: Confession at the Photo
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. At the family photograph, Dominic preempts Ngozi and admits the relationship began as a lie—but insists what grew from it did not. Adaeze's reaction is unreadable. Emotional beat: humiliation transmuted into honesty.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Ledger
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. Adaeze gives Dominic her husband's private ledger showing he was coerced by the company, having hidden evidence meant to exonerate him. 'Truth delayed is not truth denied,' she says, releasing Dominic from his silence. Emotional beat: inheritance of courage.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. At the hearing, Dominic presents the ledger and testifies; Bram speaks for the drowned and the stranded. The company's inspector cracks under cross-examination. The winter route is ordered restored. Emotional beat: justice achieved outside comfortable channels.

chapters.title: The Space Where You Were
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Victorious but hollow, Bram finds Dominic gone—back to London without goodbye, terrified that winning made the pretense unnecessary. He tends the ferry and refuses to chase. Emotional beat: heartbreak held with dignity.

chapters.title: Rewriting the Ending
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. In London, Dominic burns his safe draft and writes the true novel in nine days: two men, a lighthouse, a lie that became a vow. He mails it, then buys a ticket. Emotional beat: art and life finally aligned.

chapters.title: Before the Last Ferry
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Dominic arrives as the season's final sailing loads; Bram is aboard, leaving for winter work on the mainland. On the gangway they meet halfway, neither apologizing, both staying. The last train has already gone; it no longer matters. Emotional beat: the choice made visible.

chapters.title: Keeping the Light
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Adaeze's POV. Spring: the winter route ran all season; Dominic's novel is dedicated 'to the man who stayed.' Adaeze watches the two relight the lighthouse lamp for the tourist opening, her ledger framed on the wall. Emotional beat: found family sealed in ritual and light.
